newsitem.title: USA: Quality Dining to divest Bruegger's, take charge.
newsitem.headline: Quality Dining to divest Bruegger's, take charge.

text.p: Quality Dining Inc said Monday its board of directors approved a plan to divest the company's Bruegger's bagel-related businesses.
As a result of the divesture, the company said it expects to incur pretax charges of $140 million to $170 million for asset write-downs and overhead and staff reductions.
Quality Dining said it has terminated its Franchise Operating Partner Program, and will therefore consolidate results for Bagel Acquisition Corp into Quality Dining.

"This accounting consolidation, in conjunction with weak financial performance of the bagel business and the significant corporate general and administrative costs associated with Bruegger's, will result in a significant loss in the second quarter of fiscal 1997," the company said.
Chairman, President and Chief Executive Daniel Fitzpatrick said in a statement that the company had worked diligently to create value through the expansion of the Bruegger's brand.

"Unfortunately, the value of the Bruegger's brand to Quality Dining has deteriorated since our decision to acquire the concept in early 1996," Fitzpatrick said. "Following significant review of the various options available to the company, the management and directors of Quality Dining have determined that in order to preserve long-term shareholder value, the Bruegger's brand should be divested."
The company said it has retained Schroder Wertheim & Co to assist in the divestiture.

Quality Dining has initiated discussions with several parties, including Nordahl Brue and Michael Dressell, who are currently members of Quality Dining's board and own 4,313,326 shares of the company's outstanding common stock.

In connection with the planned divestiture of Bruegger's, Quality Dining said it suspended development of new company-owned Bruegger's units and is reviewing a potential store closure program in all company-owned markets. The company will therefore not meet its previously announced unit growth expectations, it said.

Quality Dining said as a result of its decision to divest Bruegger's, it will initiate a staff reduction program, focused primarily on Bruegger's development and training. The program is not expected to affect ongoing operations in Quality Dining's other restaurants, the company said.

"Following the planned divestiture of Bruegger's Corp, we will manage our remaining businesses with a focus on building long-term shareholder value through proven operational excellence and focused strategic growth," Fitzpatrick said.

"We believe our remaining operations represent well-established, proven concepts with outstanding long-term potential," he said. "The historical financial and operational strength of these concepts should provide a solid foundation for the company's future growth and development."
Quality Dining said Stephen Finn, Bruegger's Corp's president and chief executive and a director of Quality Dining, has resigned effective May 9.

After the planned divestiture, Quality Dining will own the Grady's American Grill, Spageddies Italian Kitchen and Papa Vino's Italian Kitchen concepts and operate Burger King restaurants and Chili's Grill & Bar restaurants as a franchisee.
